annotation.kind: direct finite-index matrix form of Theorem 2.1 and equation (2.7)

assumptions: A and W are finite complex matrices with the dimensions in Theorem 2.1.
The shift matrix J has ones on the first superdiagonal and zeros elsewhere.
The formal phi-function is the paper's series phi_ell(A)=sum_k A^k/(k+ell)!.
The finite indices are zero-based: formal column j corresponds to the paper's column j+1.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P41 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P41 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p41_t3_augmented_phi_column {n p : Nat} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Complex) (W : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin p) Complex) (tau : Complex) (ell : Nat) (j : Fin p) (i : Fin n) : p41Phi ell (tau • p41Augmented A W) (Sum.inl i) (Sum.inr j) = sum over r<j+1 of tau^(r+1) * mulVec (p41Phi (ell+r+1) (tau • A)) (p41ReverseColumn W j r) at i
formal_statement.plain_language: Every upper-right column of the phi-function of the augmented block matrix is the finite linear combination of shifted phi-functions stated in Theorem 2.1.

informal_proof: Compute every power of the augmented upper-block matrix, solve the resulting recurrence for each upper-right column, substitute that formula into the convergent phi-function series, and reindex the sums to identify each shifted phi-function.
informal_statement: Prove the full arbitrary-ell, arbitrary-p augmented-matrix column identity in Theorem 2.1, equation (2.7).

tier_rationale: The proof must establish convergence of the matrix-valued phi series, the full upper-block power recurrence, the shift-matrix column recurrence, justified reindexing of infinite sums, and a finite induction for arbitrary columns and ell. This is at least T2-level work and is not discharged by Mathlib imports. NumStability has no corresponding compiled theorem, and the exact L construction is mathematically identical to N.
